lines.text: This is a story, not a lesson. Read it and think about the people who taught you what love looks like.

groups.heading: One time I was with my grandparents

lines.text: I asked everyone to think for a second: how do you define love?
One time, I said, I was with my grandparents, and I was in high school. I went to their house because it was right next to the school. I was at a boarding school.
One day I saw them, one reading the paper on one side, the other on the other side. They would do the same thing over and over again, for years.
One day I decided to ask: Grandpa and Grandma, can you put the papers down? How do you define love between you?
They laughed and looked at me, I said, and wanted to go back to the paper. Look at this little kid asking silly questions.
But they said: Jose, it's just a feeling that you have. That's all it is. You don't talk? All you do is read the paper. They said: it doesn't matter. We feel each other's presence. That's all.
They weren't overly loving people, I said. They came from the Great Depression. They were pretty cold, very structured and regimented, black and white.

How much of that is going to influence our lives, I asked? Are we going to be people who define love and show love? What is the limit of love? Is there such a thing as showing too much love to your children, or to a husband or a wife?
How would you answer your grandparents' question?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write one person who taught you what love or care looks like.
Write how they showed it, or did not.
Write how you want to show it differently, or the same way.

check.q: What did I ask my grandparents to do?
What did they tell me love is?
choices: Just a feeling; they feel each other's presence

check.q: What question did I end with?
choices: Is there such a thing as showing too much love?

recap: Ask how the people who raised you showed love, then decide how you will.
